newsitem.title: USA: Hills Stores sees improved Q4 gross profit.
newsitem.headline: Hills Stores sees improved Q4 gross profit.

text.p: Hills Stores Co said on Thursday that it expects gross profit trends to reverse course and improve in the fourth quarter because of stronger sales trends and an aggressive fall clearance.

In last year's fourth quarter, the company reported a profit of $7.4 million, or $0.66 a share on sales of $699.8 million. Last year's fourth quarter includes a pretax charge of $9.4 million from the change in control of the company.
The company said its initiative to become more price competitive has improved sales momentum compared with softness earlier this year.
Hills Stores said the third quarter experienced increased markdowns compared with last year, because it had earlier clearance sales of fall merchandise.
Gross margin rates and gross profit dollars for the third quarter quarter will be lower than the company had aimed for, Hills Stores said.
The retailer with 165 stores said that it attempted to pursue full-priced sales deeper into the season in last year's third quarter, which led to high markdowns in last year's fourth quarter.
